name: Ellipsis

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: Environment schema: compute.cpu 2-32 vCPU (default 2), compute.memory 4 GB-64 GB (default 4 GB); compute.timeout 60 s to 1 h (default 1 h), meaning not defined further. Org compute is paid from prepaid credits that carry the 20% platform fee (multiplier 1.2).

modes.label: Own AWS VPC
modes.note: AWS infrastructure (billed by AWS) plus Ellipsis 20% platform fee; rates depend on AWS.

plans.name: Personal account
plans.note: CPU and memory are free on personal accounts; tokens via Ellipsis credits (+20% fee) or $0 when using your own Claude/Codex subscription. Only sessions you start yourself.

free.note: No sign-up credit on the pricing page; open-source maintainers get free usage case by case. Credits are prepaid, do not expire; paid requests stop when balance or a spend limit is exhausted; automatic recharge is opt-in.

caveats: Managed SaaS CPU $0.142/vCPU-hour and memory $0.024/GB-hour plus a 20% platform fee (charged on credit purchases, i.e. on token and compute spend). No per-seat or idle charges. Active lifecycle is not confirmed per-core utilization billing.
BYOC uses customer AWS compute and a 20% platform fee; cannot reuse SaaS resource rates. Support $5k/$10k/$15k per month is optional, not required plan.
YC mentions $100 credit; current pricing page did not confirm eligibility, so no unconditional free credit encoded.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.

Re-checked 2026-09-28 (ellipsis.dev/pricing, ellipsis.dev/llms.txt): Managed SaaS CPU $0.142/vCPU-h and memory $0.024/GB-h confirmed; NO published disk, snapshot or egress price, no SSH, desktop or browser statement, no sandbox size limit or billing granularity. These stay null (unknown, not free/absent).
Coding-agent platform: sandboxes run Ellipsis agent sessions (automations, @ellipsis), billed tokens + 20% platform fee (not modeled).
Session budget default $250 and hard max $250 per session; agent/handler defaults $1,000/day, $10,000/week, $40,000 per 28 days. Support packages $5,000/$10,000/$15,000 per month are optional.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

fleet.notes: API > Limits shows per-account API request limits, storage quotas, concurrency limits and spending ceilings; values are not published. Increases are requested in the shared Slack channel with the Ellipsis team or via Help.

snapshot_auto.quote: `snapshot` (saving the prepared environment for reuse), `restore` (bringing a saved environment back for a later turn)
snapshot_auto.note: Automatic, no API call: the platform snapshots the prepared environment after setup hooks and restores a saved environment when a follow-up message arrives after the sandbox went cold (conversation.warm=false). environments.md: 'A resumed session keeps its workspace, including uncommitted changes.' and 'Saved results keep files and running services' (setup-cache snapshots include running services, i.e. memory state). OpenAPI: 'Paused session workspaces have a separate lifetime'; reusable environment snapshots retained 7-28 days. Backed by Freestyle VM snapshots (OpenAPI VMImage.snapshot_id: 'Freestyle snapshot backing this reusable VM image'). Whether memory is kept for paused session workspaces is not stated.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: VMImageResponse.snapshot_id: 'Freestyle snapshot backing this reusable VM image.' Only GET operations exist for /v1/vm-images, /v1/vm-images/{image_id}, /v1/vms, /v1/vms/{vm_id} — no POST/create endpoint for images, snapshots, or forks anywhere in the spec.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Not a contradiction once checked: the only other 'snapshot' occurrence is an unrelated WebSocket frame type ('type: snapshot' = the initial session-state push on the /v1/sessions/{id}/stream socket, per llms-full.txt and docs/api/session-events.md), not a VM/disk snapshot feature. The actual VM-image snapshot mechanism (Freestyle-backed, per VMImageResponse.snapshot_id) is entirely platform-managed: images are built and cached automatically from environment setup (build_base/after_checkout hooks) and reused by cache_key; the OpenAPI spec exposes only read (GET) operations on vm-images/vms, with no user-triggered create/checkpoint/fork call. This matches feature_evidence's existing note ('only control is force_rebuild') that force_rebuild just discards the cache rather than letting the user create/name a snapshot on demand. So snapshot_on_demand=false is confirmed; snapshot_auto=true (automatic caching/restore) stands and is not in tension with it.

harness_api.quote: A session is a conversation with [Claude Code or Codex](/docs/harnesses) in its own cloud environment. The agent keeps working when you close the page or disconnect.
harness_api.note: Core product. REST API + Python/TypeScript SDKs + CLI: start a session with a prompt (claude_code or codex block), stream frames/records (native claude_jsonl / Codex events), send follow-ups (POST /v1/sessions/{id}/messages), stop turns, list/search/get sessions and turns, download transcripts, get diff/commits/PRs. Harnesses: Claude Code (incl. GLM-5.2, MiniMax M3 models) and Codex.

secret_proxy.quote: Model calls route through Ellipsis with a per-session key. A real provider key never enters an environment.
secret_proxy.note: Only model-provider credentials (Ellipsis credits or connected Claude/Codex subscription) are kept out of the sandbox via the Ellipsis LLM proxy (ELLIPSIS_LLM_PROXY_URL is a reserved variable). User secrets are plain env vars: 'The agent can read every secret its environment sets' (docs/secrets); MCP server headers get ${SECRET} substituted at session start. GitHub access uses short-lived, permission-scoped tokens minted by the GitHub App (in-sandbox). No arbitrary-host proxy; non-HTTP not covered.

isolation.quote: Freestyle VM ID, shared across session resumes. / Freestyle snapshot backing this reusable VM image.
isolation.note: Ellipsis's own OpenAPI spec identifies its sandbox backend as Freestyle VMs. Freestyle's own product page states: 'Every Freestyle VM runs on full hardware virtualization — not containers, not microVMs sharing a kernel. Each VM gets its own isolated kernel, memory, and networking stack' (full KVM support). Derived via the named subprocessor, not an Ellipsis statement of hypervisor tech.

image_oci.quote: compute.cpu | 2 to 32 vCPUs; default 2 ... hooks.build_base | Script or {run, inputs}; installs dependencies
image_oci.note: Environments are built from Ellipsis's own base image plus build_base/after_checkout setup scripts (apt/npm/pip installs); there is no field or endpoint to supply a customer Docker/OCI image.

nested_virt.note: not offered: Ellipsis's own docs/API expose only cpu/memory/timeout for a coding-agent sandbox; no /dev/kvm or nested-VM capability is documented for Ellipsis sessions (the underlying Freestyle VM supports KVM, but Ellipsis does not surface it to users).

desktop.quote: A session is a conversation with Claude Code or Codex in its own cloud environment.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Ellipsis runs headless coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code/Codex) in a sandbox; no VNC/RDP/streamed desktop is documented anywhere in the docs, dashboard, or API.

browser.note: not offered: a browser is only what a customer's own before_start hook installs (e.g. Playwright/Chromium) for running tests; Ellipsis itself does not manage or provide a browser as a platform feature.

computer_use.quote: A session is a conversation with Claude Code or Codex in its own cloud environment.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no screenshot/click driving API exists; the agent acts through file edits, shell commands, and git, not a GUI.

anti_bot.quote: Ellipsis is a cloud platform for coding agents.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — a coding-agent CI/PR platform has no stealth/fingerprinting feature.

captcha_solving.quote: Ellipsis is a cloud platform for coding agents.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CAPTCHA-solving capability is documented for this coding-agent platform.

egress_ip_type.quote: Freestyle VM ID, shared across session resumes.
egress_ip_type.note: Sandboxes run on Freestyle-backed cloud VMs (AWS-hosted per the BYOC option); no residential/mobile IP feature is documented, so outbound traffic is ordinary datacenter cloud IP space.

ssh.quote: In the dashboard, describe the task on Home and click New session. From a terminal: ellipsis --model claude-opus-5-5 -e cloud_agent_environment ...
ssh.note: not offered: Ellipsis's own docs, CLI, and OpenAPI expose only dashboard/CLI/API access to sessions (messages, records, diff, git); no SSH endpoint or credential is documented for reaching the sandbox directly.

snapshot.quote: `snapshot` (saving the prepared environment for reuse), `restore` (bringing a saved environment back for a later turn)
snapshot.note: environments.md: 'A resumed session keeps its workspace, including uncommitted changes' and 'Saved results keep files and running services' — reused/resumed environments restore running services, not just disk, so this is closer to a memory-level snapshot than a plain filesystem snapshot.

fork.note: not offered: no clone/fork endpoint exists in the OpenAPI spec (/v1/vms and /v1/vm-images are GET-only); environments are reused/rebuilt, not cloned into new independent machines.

fork_running.note: not offered: depends on fork, which is not available.

memory_snapshot_fork.note: not offered: depends on fork, which is not available; only single-machine snapshot/restore (not cloning into new running machines) is documented.

pause_resume.quote: conversation.warm | Whether an agent is ready to answer the next message right away; when false, the next message first prepares an environment, which takes longer
pause_resume.note: A conversation's sandbox goes cold (paused) when idle and is automatically restored ('warm' becomes true again) on the next message; this is automatic, not a user-invoked pause/resume API call.

wake_on_request.quote: when false, the next message first prepares an environment, which takes longer
wake_on_request.note: A cold (stopped) session automatically wakes and rebuilds its environment when a new message/request arrives.

auto_stop_idle.quote: compute.timeout | 60 seconds to 1 hour; default 1 hour
auto_stop_idle.note: Sessions/environments have a bounded timeout and go cold (non-warm) between turns/messages; there is no always-on running machine option documented.

persistent_disk.quote: A resumed session keeps its workspace, including uncommitted changes.
persistent_disk.note: Reusable environment snapshots are retained up to 28 days and files/uncommitted changes survive a session going cold and resuming.

volume_attach.note: not offered: the environment schema exposes only cpu/memory/timeout; no separate/extra persistent volume attachment is documented.

volume_shared.note: not offered: each session runs in its own isolated sandbox; no shared-volume-across-machines feature is documented.

live_resize.note: not offered: compute size is set on the environment/session config; no API to change cpu/memory of a running sandbox without a rebuild is documented.

own_agent_api.quote: A session is a conversation with Claude Code or Codex in its own cloud environment.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: Ellipsis's API drives third-party coding harnesses (Claude Code, Codex) rather than a first-party browser/computer-use/research agent of its own.

mcp_server.quote: mcp_servers | slack, linear, remote servers (name, url, headers), or local servers (name, command, args, env)
mcp_server.note: Ellipsis lets a session connect to the *user's own* MCP servers as tools; it does not ship its own MCP server for driving Ellipsis sandboxes (no mcp-server package in github.com/ellipsis-dev, only cli/sdk).

lang_python.note: Documented Python project example plus a first-party Python SDK (pip install ellipsis-dev).

lang_node.note: Documented Node.js project example plus a first-party TypeScript/npm SDK (@ellipsis-dev/sdk).

public_ipv4.quote: An environment is the repositories, setup scripts, environment variables, and machine size a session starts with.
public_ipv4.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — there is no networking/ports documentation; sandboxes are reached only via dashboard/CLI/API, not by exposing a public IP.

inbound_https.quote: An environment is the repositories, setup scripts, environment variables, and machine size a session starts with.
inbound_https.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no docs page describes exposing a URL to a port inside the sandbox.

ingress_rules.quote: An environment is the repositories, setup scripts, environment variables, and machine size a session starts with.
ingress_rules.note: not offered: depends on inbound access to the sandbox, which is not exposed.

egress_allowlist.quote: Ellipsis deletes data within 4 hours after its time to live (TTL) expires.
egress_allowlist.note: not offered: the security page covers data retention, GitHub access, secrets, and API/webhooks, with no outbound network allow/deny-list or no-internet-mode control documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: Ellipsis deletes data within 4 hours after its time to live (TTL) expires.
egress_http_rules.note: not offered: depends on egress_allowlist-level controls, which are not documented at all, let alone at HTTP method/path granularity.

guest_firewall.quote: sudo apt-get update / sudo apt-get install -y jq
guest_firewall.note: derived: build_base hooks run with sudo/root inside a full VM-backed sandbox, so nftables/iptables would work; not explicitly documented by Ellipsis itself.

static_egress_ip.quote: Ellipsis deletes data within 4 hours after its time to live (TTL) expires.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: no fixed/static outbound IP is documented anywhere on the site or docs.

gpu.quote: compute.cpu | 2 to 32 vCPUs; default 2 / compute.memory | 4096MB to 64GB; default 4096MB
gpu.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — the compute schema only exposes cpu and memory for a coding-agent sandbox; no GPU option is documented.

windows.quote: an isolated Linux machine created for that session with the repositories cloned in
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Ellipsis explicitly describes its sandbox as a Linux machine; no Windows machine option exists.

macos.quote: an isolated Linux machine created for that session with the repositories cloned in
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — sandboxes are Linux-only; no macOS machine option exists.

self_host.quote: Can everything stay in our own cloud? Yes. Ellipsis is self-hostable in your AWS account, so credentials and code never leave your VPC.
self_host.note: Marketed as 'self-hostable' into the customer's own AWS account (the card's byoc mode).

open_source.note: The github.com/ellipsis-dev org publishes only the CLI, SDK, and a homebrew tap under MIT; the core platform/agent-runner is closed source and only offered as a hosted or self-hosted (in customer AWS) managed service.

hipaa.quote: SOC 2 Type I Certified, SOC 2 Type II In progress ... Scoped credentials ... Zero source retention ... Full audit trail
hipaa.note: not offered: the enterprise/security pages enumerate compliance features in detail (SOC 2, scoped credentials, zero source retention, audit trail) but never mention HIPAA eligibility or a BAA.

sso.quote: Owners and admins change spending settings while signed in; API keys and session credentials can't change them.
sso.note: not offered: the organization/account-settings docs describe owners/admins and API keys but never mention SAML/OIDC SSO.

eu_data_residency.quote: 215 Park Ave S, Floor 11, Suite 42, New York, NY 10003
eu_data_residency.note: not offered: Ellipsis AI Inc. is a US (New York) company; no regions or EU-hosting option is documented anywhere in the docs or pricing pages.

max_session_h.quote: compute.timeout | 60 seconds to 1 hour; default 1 hour
max_session_h.note: Each turn is capped at a configurable timeout of at most 1 hour; interactive sessions can continue across many turns/follow-ups (with the sandbox going cold and auto-resuming between them), but no single continuous machine run exceeds this per-turn 1-hour ceiling.

arm64.quote: Freestyle VMs are x86_64 Linux, so the VM needs the **`linux-amd64`** release — the `darwin-arm64` tarball you may already have installed locally is a Mach-O binary and will not execute there.
arm64.note: Ellipsis sandboxes run on Freestyle VMs (confirmed in the card's own feature_evidence: 'Backed by Freestyle VM snapshots'); Freestyle's own docs state its VMs are x86_64 Linux only, with a further confirming line elsewhere in the same doc: `console.log(uname.stdout.trim()); // Linux … 6.1.0-15-freestyle … x86_64`. No ARM/aarch64 machine option is offered on Ellipsis's own docs, pricing, or OpenAPI spec.

cpu_class.quote: vCPU, memory and storage are all billed on the amount allocated to the VM for the time it is allocated — a reserved core is yours whether or not the guest is busy.
cpu_class.note: derived: Ellipsis's own OpenAPI spec identifies its sandbox backend as Freestyle VMs (VMImageResponse.snapshot_id: 'Freestyle snapshot backing this reusable VM image'), the same subprocessor the card's own isolation field is derived from. Ellipsis's pricing page bills CPU by vCPU-hour on a per-vCPU allocation basis ($0.142/vCPU-hour, cpu_basis: alloc in the card) consistent with Freestyle's own published billing model, which states cores are reserved/dedicated once allocated to a VM rather than shared/oversubscribed. Ellipsis itself does not use the words 'dedicated' or 'shared' anywhere in its docs/pricing, so this is inferred via the named infrastructure subprocessor, not a direct Ellipsis statement. Not resolved for the 'byoc' mode, since that mode runs on the customer's own AWS account/instance type, which Ellipsis's docs do not specify.

usage_api.quote: Read usage for a UTC calendar month. Rated subscription usage is separate from actual Ellipsis credit charges. [Response includes] total_cost_millicents
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: yes; GET /v1/account/usage endpoint available via REST API, Python SDK (account.usage()), and TypeScript SDK. Returns usage broken down by model, daily, developer (attribution), and funding source for a calendar month.
